request: Ahri’s orb damages a stationary enemy repeatedly while passing through it. It should hit each enemy once going outward and once returning, regardless of simulation step size. Reproduce the issue and investigate what is causing it.
analysis: Source inspection identifies a likely cause in DexArena.StepShots: collision eligibility checks m.hit.Contains(u), but the collision handler clears m.hit instead of recording the struck unit. The orb remains active after collisions, so successive simulation ticks may damage the same overlapping target. The separate clear at the outward-to-return transition appears intended to permit one additional hit on return. This remains a hypothesis until execution. The scenario compares fine and coarse steps, checks outward and completed-flight damage separately, and includes an off-path enemy control. With AP 0 and target MR 100, one outward hit deals 50 magic damage and one return hit deals 100 true damage.

reviewReason: The report explicitly requires one hit per enemy per direction, independent of step size. Original source sets orb damage to 100 + 0.5*AP: with AP 0 and MR 100, one outward magic hit deals 50 and one returning true-damage hit deals 100. These preserve existing per-hit balance, yielding 150 total damage. All setup occurs before casting. The trace reproduces excess damage: fine steps deal 450 outward and 1650 total; coarse steps deal 300 total. StepShots clears the hit set on collision without adding the victim, permitting repeated overlap hits. Retained damage and off-path controls directly witness the report; equality across step sizes alone would also accept equally broken results. These checks cover the supplied stationary-target scenario, not all enemies or step sizes.

patchExplanation: The supplied arena run reproduces repeated hits: the fine-step flight dealt 1650 total damage, while the coarse-step flight dealt 300. StepShots checks m.hit.Contains(u), but clears that set on every collision and never records the victim. Record each hit instead. The existing clear when the orb turns around then permits one new hit per enemy on return, preserving damage values and collision geometry. This proposal requires host verification against the frozen scenario.
